rows.text: The passages say that certain high-risk categories of machinery require a conformity assessment procedure with a notified body (Recital 59, REG), but they do not list those categories. Annex VII, IX, or X of the Regulation, which the passages mention but do not reproduce, would need to be consulted.

value: EU type-examination (module B) followed by conformity to type based on internal production control (module C)
conformity based on full quality assurance (module H)
conformity based on unit verification (module G)
rows.text: For machinery in Annex I, Part A, the manufacturer (or the person referred to in Article 18) must choose one of three procedures under Article 25(2): module B followed by module C (Annexes VII and VIII), module H (Annex IX), or module G (Annex X). Article 6(1) confirms that Part A categories are subject to the Article 25(2) procedures.

value: Annex I, Part A, point 5 (safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches ensuring safety functions)
rows.text: Such a safety component falls under Annex I, Part A, point 5 of the REG. Recital 54 explains that these systems are included in Annex I and need third-party conformity assessment, and Recital 55 confirms that these provisions apply to them.

rows.value: Interlocking movable guards are required (under the Regulation, Annex III, 1.3.8.1, 'shall') where frequent access is envisaged. The Directive (Annex I, 1.3.8.1) says they 'should' be used in that case. Otherwise, fixed guards are permitted.
rows.text: Under Annex III, section 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation, interlocking movable guards shall be used where frequent access to the moving transmission parts is envisaged; the Directive's Annex I, section 1.3.8.1 says they should be used in that case. Section 3.4.2 provides an engine-compartment exception for guards that are opened only by a tool, key, or a control in a locked, fully enclosed driving cab.

The passages do not include the text of Annex III, point 1.3.7, so they cannot say which risks it addresses. Passage 4 gives only the heading for point 1.3 (Protection against mechanical risks), not the sub-point itself.

rows.value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification of the machinery (a non-professional user modifying their own machinery for their own use is excluded)
rows.text: Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation, the natural or legal person who carries out a substantial modification is treated as the manufacturer and must meet the Article 10 manufacturer obligations, including declaring conformity on its sole responsibility. A non-professional user who modifies their own machinery for their own use is not considered a manufacturer under this Article.

value: EC declaration of conformity (DIR Art. 5(1)(e), Annex II Part 1 Section A)
EU declaration of conformity (REG Art. 10(8), referenced in Art. 15(2)(b) and 13(2))
Instructions for use and the information referred to in REG Art. 10(7)
rows.text: Under the Directive, the manufacturer must ensure the EC declaration of conformity accompanies the machinery (Art. 5(1)(e)). Under the Regulation, the machinery must be accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity (Art. 15(2)(b), Art. 13(2)) and by the instructions for use and the information in Art. 10(7) (Art. 15(2)(c)).

Manufacturers must keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for 10 years after the product is placed on the market, as stated in Article 7(3) of Directive 2014/30/EU, Article 6(3) of Directive 2014/34/EU, Article 6(3) of Directive 2014/35/EU, Article 6(3) of Directive 2014/68/EU, Article 10(3) of the Machinery Regulation, Article 8(3) of Regulation (EU) 2016/425, and Article 9(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/988. Article 10(3) of the Machinery Regulation says 'at least 10 years' and requires the documents to be available to market surveillance authorities.
The passages do not include Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 or its application article, so they do not give its date of application.

No. Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from 14 January 2027 (Art. 51(2) of the Regulation). The transitional rule in Art. 52(1) protects only products placed on the market in conformity with that Directive before 14 January 2027, so it does not cover new placing on 16 January 2027. The passages do not expressly say that new placing is prohibited, only that the protection is limited to products placed before that date.

rows.value: INAIL carries out the first periodic verification, within 45 days of the request (45 days from receipt of a complete request)
rows.text: Under Article 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008, the employer uses INAIL for the first periodic verification of the equipment in Annex VII, and INAIL must carry it out within 45 days of the request. The INAIL guide specifies that the 45 days run from receipt of the complete request, and that they are suspended if INAIL reports missing mandatory information.

The EU directive (Art. 5(3)) requires inspection results to be kept for a suitable period, without specifying a length. The Italian provision in the UNICT guideline (p. 18, comma 9 of art. 71) requires that at least the results from the last three years be kept and available to supervisory authorities.

The passages do not identify any product catalogue, model list, or 20 January 2027 transition date, so they cannot show which models would need a notified body. Annex III point 3 and point 4 of Directive 2014/68/EU describe notified-body sampling of final assessment, but they do not link that to any self-certified models.

The passages do not mention model RC-5 or any requirement taking effect on 20 January 2027, so they cannot identify which conformity assessment procedure it will need or why. The passages cover general procedures under Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2016/425, Article 25 of the Machinery Regulation, and Article 13 of Directive 2014/34/EU, but none apply them to RC-5.

The passages describe Module A internal production control in several directives and regulations, but none names model CS-400 or sets a 20 January 2027 cut-off, so they cannot say whether CS-400 can stay under that procedure after that date. Check the applicable legal text and transitional provisions for that date.

The provided passages do not list the categories in Annex I, Part A of the Regulation or the contents of Annex IV to Directive 2006/42/EC, so the comparison cannot be made. Article 6(1) of the Regulation only states that Annex I, Part A categories are subject to the procedures in Article 25(2).

No. Article 16(1) of Directive 2014/33/EU limits lifts to final inspection (Annex V), conformity to type (Annexes X or XII), unit verification (Annex VIII), or full quality assurance plus design examination (Annex XI). Internal production control is not among them, and the presumption of conformity under Article 14 and Recital 18 does not replace a required procedure. The passages do not mention the 20 January 2027 date.

The passages do not mention any essential requirement on protection against corruption. They only explain that Directive 2006/42/EC was replaced by a regulation so that the essential health and safety requirements apply uniformly (Recital 4), so the question cannot be answered from them.

The passages do not state which article of the Regulation corresponds to Article 12 of Directive 2006/42/EC. Article 51(2) says references to the repealed Directive are to be read in accordance with the correlation table in Annex XII of the Regulation, but that table's contents are not included in the passages.

The passages do not give the mapping. Article 51(2) says references to Directive 2006/42/EC are to be read against the correlation table in Annex XII of the Regulation, but that table's contents are not in the passages. The Annex VI and X correlation tables provided cover other directives.

The passages do not give the verification interval for the DEMAG overhead travelling crane at position 8. Position 8 falls under table A2 of Allegato A, but that table's contents are not included. Passage 1 says all 24 positions follow the Allegato VII frequencies of D.Lgs. 81/08, and passage 8 lists those frequencies by crane type, age and use, but the passages don't establish which category the DEMAG crane falls into. Table A2 or the equipment record would be needed.

value: P1Y (annual, if the crane is used in a particular sector such as estrattivo/mining or costruzioni)
P2Y (biennial, if used in other sectors, since a 2017 build is not yet more than 10 years old)
rows.text: The IGEA technical sheet places truck-mounted cranes (positions 1-7) under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08. For a mobile crane over 200 kg built within the last 10 years, the rule is annual verification in particular sectors (construction, steel, port, mining) and biennial verification in other sectors. Position 7's sector is not stated in the passages, and its table A1 entry is not included, so the exact interval cannot be confirmed.

rows.value: After the first verification, the employer freely chooses the ASL (local health authority) or, where regional law provides, ARPA, or an authorised public or private body (soggetto pubblico o privato abilitato).
rows.text: Under art. 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008, subsequent periodic verifications of Annex VII equipment are carried out, at the employer's free choice, by the ASL or, where regional law provides, by ARPA, or by authorised public or private bodies. The inail-guide (p. 35) repeats this for the SP group.

rows.value: 45 days under Legislative Decree 81/2008 art. 71(11) and the INAIL guide; 60 days under DM 11 April 2011 art. 2(1). The passages do not say which prevails.
rows.text: Article 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 says INAIL must carry out the first periodic verification within 45 days of the request, and the INAIL guide (p. 36 and p. 40) repeats the 45-day deadline. Article 2(1) of the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011 says 60 days. The passages do not resolve which figure binds, so the statute's 45 days is the figure the INAIL guide follows.

Per section 3.2.1 (p. 20), the UR5e is 'partly completed machinery' and comes with a Declaration of Incorporation, and a risk assessment is required for each robot application. Section 'About this manual' (p. 4) also says to perform a risk assessment and install and use the robot as specified, so it is not presented as ready for use on its own.

The nanoScan3 must undergo the regular thorough check at least once a year, including the principal function test and the detection capability (resolution) test (manual p. 51, section 5.6.2). The risk assessment may require more frequent checks, and daily checks of the principal function are recommended in many cases.

The verifier must plan the checks jointly with IGEA's appointed staff and give IGEA at least 15 days' advance notice, as stated in section 4 (Impegni Aggiudicatario/Verificatore) of the igea-equipment Scheda Tecnica, p. 5.

Position 13 is an overhead travelling crane listed in table A2 (passage 0), and the interval is set by Allegato VII (passage 7). The passages do not state whether this crane is fixed or mobile, its sector of use, or its table A2 entry, all of which determine the interval, so it cannot be determined from them. The 2017 build year matters only for the rows split by whether the equipment is more or less than 10 years old.

The passages do not give the verification interval for the overhead travelling crane at position 13 (table A2, positions 8-13). Passage 1 says all 24 positions follow the periodicity in Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08, but the Allegato VII excerpt in passage 8 is cut off before the lifting-apparatus entries, so no specific frequency or build-year rule is stated.

The passages place the elevating platform at position 24 (table A6, Allegato A) and say its verification follows the periodicities in Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08, art. 2.3 of the technical specification. They do not state the specific interval, and they do not name HINOWA or include table A6.

The passages place position 8 in table A2 of Allegato A (overhead travelling cranes, positions 8-13), but table A2 and its last-verification dates are not included, so the DEMAG crane's status cannot be determined. Consult Allegato A, table A2 of the IGEA technical specification, and the verification records.
The UR10e reach is 1300 mm (passage 0, p. 15) and the UR5e reach is 850 mm (passage 6, p. 15), so replacing the UR5e with a UR10e increases reach by 450 mm.
The wear indicator of the load nut on the MA STAR 3.5 A must be checked every 6 months, per section 7.3 (Checking the Load Nut's Wear Indicator) of the MA STAR operating instructions.

The passages show that the residual life cycles structural verification certificate is required only for equipment older than 20 years (Passage 0, point 5 of the documentation list). They also place position 8 among the overhead travelling cranes (gru a ponte scorrevole, positions 8-13, table A2). They do not give the age of the DEMAG crane at position 8, so whether the certificate is needed cannot be determined from these passages. The age would be in table A2 of Allegato A, which is not included.
